Carrier existence is provider-documented; the span and the value policy are project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-06 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence#242. Question: Can an admin-role positive be asserted when the x-algolia-api-key header is shared by every Algolia key role, including the frontend-safe search-only key? Options: Flag the header value on any request; flag it only on the create-key request whose documented requirement attributes the role; or author no positive. Decision: Flag the header value on the create-key request only. No bare-value rule and no expectation for the same header on other endpoints. Reason: The create-key endpoint is the one place Algolia states the key must be an admin key, and the admin key's confidentiality is documented; the header on other endpoints is shared with a key documented as safe in frontend code, so a header-only rule would contradict the contract. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's explicit instruction of 2026-10-06 (complete redact-secret#1228, #1229 and #1230 before the next release; Cases for these groups are authored maintainer-only, as in Batch 2).
events.dissent: No dissent was raised. The strongest counter-argument, recorded because the rule asks for one: The D1 handoff concluded a role-specific must-flag cannot be authored because the carrier is shared; the pages state no value format, so a position-only rule can flag a non-secret or miss a differently shaped value, and a request that is not a create-key request cannot be told from one by the value.
events.reversingEvidence: An Algolia statement that the header carries other values on the create-key endpoint or of the key format, a documented marker that separates admin keys from other keys, or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes it.
